title: Mixed feelings greet award: Constable's bullet saved pharmacist
article: A Calgary police officer who shot and killed a knife-wielding man during a downtown hostage taking will receive a national award for bravery and excellence for saving the life of a local pharmacist.

Two other Calgary officers who pulled an unconscious man from a burning home in the city's southwest last year will pick up provincial awards of excellence at this year's Canadian Police Association ceremony in Quebec City.
The trio will collect their awards at a banquet Aug. 31.

Const. Julien Gagne, a rookie in the Calgary police department, shot 34-year-old Arthur George Provencal in the head as he held a knife to the throat of a pharmacist during a bungled robbery Dec. 23. Provencal -- who was on release from Drumheller Institution at the time -- refused to drop his weapon when ordered by Gagne. The officer had entered the TD Square Shoppers Drug Mart thinking there had been a robbery and was unaware of the hostage situation. He fired one shot at Provencal, hitting him between the eyes.
Gagne, 25, said he has mixed feelings about receiving the award. He's proud to receive the national honour but the situation was regrettable.

"It is very strange and it's unfortunate. I don't think anyone wants to go through something like this, but (under the) circumstances, I don't think I had any other recourse," said Gagne. "I think (my family) is pretty proud of me. I've had nothing but support from everybody."
Gagne, originally from Manitoba, returned to work about a month after the shooting. A police internal investigation into the shooting is ongoing.
After the shooting, Provencal's family argued the man who begged the pharmacist for a lethal dose of drugs that night in the store was a decent person struggling with addiction.

"My uncle chose the wrong path and could not help himself, nor could he be helped," said Provencal's nephew Mark Saikaly. "Beneath all the pain, suffering and confusion was a man just like anyone else, and that is how I will remember him."
Gagne is the second Calgary police officer in four years selected as the National Recipient of the Canadian Police Association Awards of Excellence -- the highest award given by the association.

"The intended victim's family, his children, wrote Christmas cards to Const. Gagne thanking him for ensuring that their father would be there for Christmas," said Calgary Police Association president Al Koenig.
"(Julien's) a tremendous asset to our department for being a complete package."
There are hundreds of nominees countrywide for the excellence awards with only a handful of winners selected every year.

Const. Shane Plamondon and Sgt. Mike Lomore, both District 2 officers, will receive provincial awards from the Canadian association for pulling Chris Laughren from the basement of his burning home at 2703 Lionel Cres. S.W.
Laughren had run back into his house with a garden hose to extinguish the flames when he passed out.
Lomore and Plamondon were the first to arrive and after learning the man was inside, the pair crawled along the hose and pulled Laughren from the home.
"(We) didn't really say anything, we just looked at each other and went into the house," said Plamondon, a three-year member of the force.
"I never thought I would be involved in something like that, let alone get an award for it."
Koenig said the pair's actions are just another instance of police officers doing what needs to be done in the heat of the moment.

"They went above and beyond and put themselves at tremendous risk by going into a burning building," said Koenig. "That's the stuff that heroes are made of, especially in the case of all three of these guys."
